I had a very positive experience with two of the doctors at Hedingham Medical Centre previously. Supportive, caring and professional. Their service could not be faulted and I was very grateful to be seen with such promptness.

An improvement, however, could be seen in displaying more consistent listening skills across the receptionist team. I felt that some staff members have frequently and abruptly interrupted me to rush to a solution - on the phone and in person - while I have been trying to explain a situation; this has been quite frustrating and has resulted in my having to re-explain and chase results in my own time.

The results which I chased were going to be ‘put on the digital system’. We drove to my old surgery, requested a print out of the blood results and drove back to Hedingham Medical Centre, delivering these very results by hand and were assured that these would be reviewed by a doctor. Whether that happened cannot be confirmed as nothing was ever viewable on the online record. I ended up having to have a repeat blood test which was frustrating after investing lots of time into accessing the previous results. The staff didn’t really seem to care. After several attempts to find out the results, I told the receptionist staff that I was just about ready to give up due to having so many obstacles. One of the receptionist team replied ‘so I don’t have to bother with this then?’. Pretty much sums up my whole two-month experience so far.

I have also been told quite unprofessionally by reception and admin staff that ‘things take time’ when asked on several occasions to view historical medical data (on the same system!) and to have access to my baby’s online account to view vaccination data. It will almost have been a two-month wait… compared to our previous surgery with the same ‘systm online’ account who set it up within two minutes before my very eyes… and access was immediate so I know it can definitely be done ! The reception staff are very quick to talk over you and shut you down at the Hedingham Medical Centre. It has been such a frustrating experience so far.

Reception staff also talk about you, your full name and your medical situation by shouting across the office for all of the waiting room to hear - I’ve never seen anything like it.

Whilst it is fully appreciated that a public role is demanding, I remain hopeful that listening without interruption and displaying some degree of elegance when dealing with patients will help all parties in the long run. Having been witness to other conversations when in the waiting room, however, I unfortunately don’t hold out much hope for any meaningful change.

The reception and admin staff very much let down the medical staff at the Hedingham Medical Centre.
